notes: Timestral-209M time-series forecaster for LiteRT (mlboydaisuke/Timestral-209M-LiteRT, Hub revision 11f5cc3534dcdd6cfbb6ccb6f462c733e468b0b0, uploaded 2026-10-23): mistralai/Timestral-209M (revision 9874d252, Modified MIT License, Mistral AI) re-implemented with fixed shapes from mistralai/timestral a534bdbd (Apache-2.0) and converted with litert-torch 0.9.4, one graph per size: the patch embedding, the 24 transformer layers and the quantile head in one call, one signature serving_default, five float32 inputs (patches [2,L,64], dec [2,H,768], bias [1,1,S,S], cos / sin [1,1,S,64]) and one float32 output (output_0 [2,H,32,21], the normalized quantiles); 2 rows = the series and its negation, L context and H decoder patches of 32 steps, S = L + H; the host code in the repository (Python, Kotlin) runs the official forecaster's steps around the call. Four sizes (c2048 = L 64, c8192 = L 256; h256 = H 8, h1024 = H 32), each a float16-weight file (the GPU at FP16 precision; the c2048 ones also the Qualcomm NPU) and an -int8 file (the CPU: ai-edge-quantizer 0.9.0 dynamic-range int8 on the fully connected layers of the first 23 of the 24 blocks). The float16-range rewrites (every RMSNorm input pre-scaled by a power of two, the attention logits at 1/16 with the row maximum subtracted, the softmax input clamped at -3e4, the mask value -3e4) leave float32 results unchanged. artifact_sha256 = the Hub LFS sha256 (API read 2026-10-23 16:07 JST) = the upload list = the bytes the phone ran (the hold's sha256 read-back, MATCH). The check set: 84 fixture windows (72 from UCI Air Quality, Datadog BOOM and UCI ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014, 12 synthetic; horizons 24 to 720 steps); a phone run runs the windows of its file's size. Paths: M/ = timestral/ of the zoo worktree (branch timestral). Records written 2026-10-23 by the run-9 generator (source). This file: timestral-209m-c8192-h256.tflite (405,041,792 B), the GPU (FP16) file for contexts of up to 8,192 steps and horizons of up to 256 steps; kept off the NPU (other forms of these graphs took 82.0 to 96.5 ms per forecast on the HTP against 68.7 to 73.4 ms for these files on the GPU).
quantization: float16 weights (ai-edge-quantizer 0.9.0); float32 inputs and output

evidence: gate app com.mlboydaisuke.d1omni.gate in generic mode (Kotlin CompiledModel, LiteRT 2.2.0; debug build r9), one cold process per run, the fixture rows pushed as raw float32 tensors (the host steps done on the Mac); measured interval = the five input writes + run + the output read-back per call. Holds s4 and t4 of 2026-10-22.

forecast check vs the official TimestralForecaster.forecast() (PyTorch, float32, CPU, every default) on the 5 fixture windows of this size (contexts of 2,049 to 8,192 steps, horizons of up to 256 steps; 2 groups): MASE 0.432961 vs 0.432953 (ratio x1.000020), CRPS 0.125659 vs 0.125656 (ratio x1.000017); NaN / inf 0, quantile order broken 0, graph inputs equal to the host's 5 / 5; the bar (both ratios <= 1.01, no NaN / inf, the 21 quantiles in order at every step): PASS.

output_match = the shared element rule (|out - ref| <= max(1e-05, 0.001 * |ref|) per element, litert_compat.probe.runners.Tolerance) against the same file on the Mac CPU on the same rows (ai-edge-litert 2.2.0 XNNPACK, 8 threads; the vs_mac.cpu block): every one of the 5 rows is bit-equal (max |d| 0) -> True.
